analyzed_vuln.description: `ndpi_reset_packet_line_info()` clears the packet-scoped HTTP line pointers but omits `content_disposition_line.ptr` and `.len`. That field points directly into the current packet payload. After a packet containing a `Content-Disposition` header is processed, `ndpi_detection_process_packet()` calls this incomplete reset and the harness frees the packet buffer, leaving the flow's packet structure with a dangling nonzero `content_disposition_line`. On a later HTTP extra packet, `ndpi_http_check_content()` trusts the stale length and performs a 3-byte `memcmp` through the freed pointer at http.c:149. The patch should reset both members alongside all other packet-line fields.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A multi-packet TCP flow must first parse an HTTP packet containing a sufficiently long `Content-Disposition: ...` value, causing `ndpi_parse_packet_line_info()` to store a pointer into that packet buffer. HTTP detection must retain extra-packet processing. After the caller releases that first packet buffer, a later packet on the same flow must re-enter the HTTP dissector and reach content checking (in this PoV it supplies a nonempty `Content-Type`/HTTP header context). Because the incomplete reset preserves the old disposition length and pointer, the executable-extension scan indexes the freed prior-packet data and calls `memcmp(..., 3)`.
